winterStorage.note: LL-33 experimental game balance. Feed: about 9.5 lb/cu ft for small square hay bales (~50 lb in 5.25 cu ft) and 40 lb/cu ft for bagged poultry feed; 10 cu ft of household bins without a shed. Above-ground tanks freeze after their freezing degree-days (°F below 32, accumulated; thaw days melt) — bigger tanks hold out longer; the pond and Earthship cisterns are treated as frost-protected. Insulation multiplies the tolerance by 4; a thermostatic heater draws kWh per gallon per freezing degree-day.

LL-34 experimental balance from the catalog row: 30 lb of green biomass per 2.1 h is about 14 lb/h, 2.4× the 6 lb/h of hand-cut wild greens. Applies to green biomass only, not foraged food.
LL-34 experimental balance. The catalog row (20 lb per 0.5 h) would imply 13× a 3 lb/h clay bank, but a broadfork loosens beds rather than digging clay, so the boost is capped at 2×.

soilFertility.note: LL-35 experimental game balance. Fertility 1 is the catalog's full yield; yield = 30% + 70% × fertility, capped at 110%. A full year of cropping draws 0.35 (annual beds) or 0.15 (perennials), scaled by realized yield; the catalog's own compost rate replaces exactly that draw. Bought-soil beds start at 1, dug-in plots at 0.7, perennial plantings at 0.8. A pound of manure counts as half a pound of compost. A clover cover crop adds 0.2 a year to gardens within 100 ft, shared by their area.
